doesRT27GATEsFRAMINGSURVIVETHEv28TERMINA.theRule: Resolution terminates at a full-text standalone's reviewed bytes; full-chain resolution would discard the only reviewed bytes in the chain.
doesRT27GATEsFRAMINGSURVIVETHEv28TERMINA.answer: YES, and better than 'survives'. RT27-GATE's refusal is at the DECLARATION stage -- two names, two digests -- which is one step BEFORE any recursion question arises. The termination rule disposes of v26's change-log false positive; it does not touch v27's declaration form. So the finding stands unchanged.
doesRT27GATEsFRAMINGSURVIVETHEv28TERMINA.andTHEINSTRUMENTALREADYIMPLEMENTSTHERULE: MEASURED, and this is the most creditable thing in the file. resolve_subject IS recursive -- it calls itself on a predecessor that declares a derivation. I measured what it actually does with v26: prov['predecessorIsItselfADerivation'] is FALSE, no 'via' key is produced, and find_declaration(v26) returns None with ZERO errors. It binds v26 at canonical digest 546abee0..., which I independently computed from v26's own reviewed bytes and confirmed identical. It does not recurse; it does not discard the reviewed bytes; it does not replace them with a reconstruction from v25. Written in August, this instrument reached the answer the v28 review would not articulate until 2026-08-10, and its comment at lines 759-763 gives the right reason in the right words: 'A historical log with only a predecessor byte digest is data inside a standalone artifact, not a request to replace that artifact with a recursively materialised value.'
doesRT27GATEsFRAMINGSURVIVETHEv28TERMINA.theHONESTCAVEAT: It terminates for the RIGHT REASON stated in prose but by the WRONG MECHANISM in code. The terminus is a side effect of the two-digest screen (`if not names or len(set(digests)) < 2: continue`), not an explicit test of whether the predecessor is reviewed. The v28 review's rule is 'the terminus test is the REVIEW, not the SHAPE'. This instrument's terminus test IS the shape. A future predecessor whose change-log happened to carry two distinct digests would be recursed into, and reviewed bytes WOULD be discarded. Correct today, structurally fragile. Filed as OBS-RT27R-01, non-blocking, because it is right on these bytes and its own prose already states the correct rule.

The second implementation is real. Only its denominator is ungated.
nonBlockingFindings.bound: Not reachable through the delta alone -- `evictableCount` lives in the GATED predecessor and an operation cannot delete or retype a leaf (RT27-DERIV-TYPE, RT27-DERIV-NONSCALAR). It is reachable by any future successor in this lineage. Non-blocking on these bytes; a live trap for the next one.

nonBlockingFindings.title: The mutation suite exercises 16 of the 50 distinct RT27-* codes the file can emit, is hand-enumerated, and publishes no coverage figure.
nonBlockingFindings.detail: 38 cases, 0 build failures, 0 no-op mutations, every case a WRONG input rather than an EMPTY one, delta discipline enforced per-family -- the suite is well built. But 34 codes are never driven by it, including RT27-XCHECK (the second implementation), RT27-CLOSURE (the coverage gates), RT27-ANCHOR, and every resolver refusal branch (RT27-DERIV-VERB, -NONSCALAR, -PATH, -PARENT, -ABSENT, -NO-TO, -OPCOUNT, -FLOAT, -AMBIGUOUS, -AMBIGUOUS-OPERATIONS, -AMBIGUOUS-PREDECESSOR).
nonBlockingFindings.freezeSection: 7.2.2, sharpened 2026-08-10: 'a lane that does not publish how many rows it generated is not making a weaker claim -- it is making an uncheckable one', and 'derive the row set from the artifact's own structure, and publish the count of rows generated, so a reader can tell coverage from luck.'
nonBlockingFindings.mitigation: I drove RT27-XCHECK, RT27-CLOSURE, RT27-ANCHOR, RT27-DRIVER, RT27-PIN-RESURRECTED, RT27-PIN-REFUSED, RT27-INPUT-MISSING, RT27-PARSE-REFUSED and RT27-UNSUPPORTED-INVOCATION externally and all nine fire correctly and non-vacuously. The gap is in the suite's self-account, not in the guards.

nonBlockingFindings.title: E8 is published as an escape and is NOT one. The instrument understates itself.
nonBlockingFindings.detail: E8 claims 'Move $.whatIDidNotCheck from seven honest entries to one, or to zero. A shrinking limitations list is invisible to this run.' Measured: truncating the list to one entry produces FOUR new findings, because check_census re-walks the delta file's own leaf census from the written bytes and the removed entries change it. The disclosure is gated -- by the census, not by anything aimed at it, but gated. 7.2 names this failure mode as the rare one worth naming: a candidate consistently wrong in the direction of understating itself is invisible to ordinary scepticism.

nonBlockingFindings.title: 31% of the delta file is walk-visible but UNADDRESSABLE by the instrument's own path grammar.
nonBlockingFindings.detail: 561 of 1811 scalar leaves live under $.corpusChecksRun.perCheckerRecord.<filename>.py.<field>, where the object keys are FILENAMES containing dots. path_steps() splits on '.', so no path string the instrument generates for that block can be fed back through get_path(). scalar_leaves() and census() still WALK it correctly (they are walkers, not parsers), so the census figures are right -- but referent_sweep's round trip `get_path(predecessor, f"{path}.measuredValues")` is structurally blind inside it, and no future referent row could ever reach it either.
nonBlockingFindings.relationToE4: E4 already names $.corpusChecksRun as 'the largest single unbound surface in the artifact, at several hundred leaves'. This sharpens it: the block is not merely unread, it is unaddressable, so the fix is not 'add rows' but 'change the path grammar or the artifact's key shape'.
nonBlockingFindings.notADEFECTTODAY: No finding depends on addressing that block, and I found no wrong answer caused by it. Recorded because a reader would otherwise assume the sweep could be extended there.

nonBlockingFindings.title: --selftest returns before the 7.2.1 post-run re-measurement, so RT27-TREE-MOVED cannot fire in selftest mode.
nonBlockingFindings.detail: main() computes `before = measure_all_inputs()` at line 2906 and `after = ...` at line 3019, but the selftest branch returns at 3009/3012/3014, above it. A 69-second selftest is the longest window the instrument has and it is the one window with no concurrency guard.

nonBlockingFindings.title: 'invariants 24/24 executed' counts DRIVERS DISPATCHED, not invariants verified.
nonBlockingFindings.detail: In the executed reference, `executed += 1` precedes the driver call unconditionally over a frozen 24-id literal; a driver that raises KeyError/TypeError/IndexError still increments it, though it also emits a named RT26-INV finding. The vector counter is stricter -- `if row is None: continue` precedes the increment. Both are paired with missing/invented id checks measuring 0/0, so on these bytes 24/24 is true in the strong sense as well. Recorded so the number is read correctly.

nonBlockingFindings.title: Two banner figures are literals rather than counts.
nonBlockingFindings.detail: ctx['keyLocatorDirections'] = 6 is assigned as a constant at line 1303 and printed as 'keyLocator: 6 directions executed'; the banner header prints 'destroyed 1' as a literal rather than len(). Both are true of these bytes -- the six directions do all execute unconditionally, and there is one destroyed pin -- so neither is a false statement. They are figures a reader would take for measurements and cannot recompute from the run.

nonBlockingFindings.title: The DESTROYED class is a one-entry literal -- but unlike the sibling it was faulted for, it is DIGEST-keyed and swept over the whole directory.
nonBlockingFindings.detail: 7.10's rider faults check-retention-custody-v25.py for `if name in UNSATISFIABLE_PINS`, a one-entry literal keyed by NAME, violating 'standing is DISCOVERED, not listed'. Here DESTROYED_DIGEST is also a single literal, but the guard is keyed by CONTENT and swept over EVERY file under artifacts/, not merely DESTROYED_PATH -- and check_recorded_inputs compares it against the artifact's own destroyed[] rows in BOTH directions, so a second destroyed row would be a finding. The residual: the SWEEP SET is not derived from the artifact, so a second declared destroyed digest would be reported as a class mismatch and would NOT be swept for. Narrow, and materially better than the sibling.
nonBlockingFindings.nonVacuityPROVEN: External driver, shipped file imported unmodified, only the driver's copy of the constant re-pointed at a file that exists. Control: no refusal. Probe: PinRefused carrying RT27-PIN-RESURRECTED, naming retention-tiers.v28.json -- a file at a COMPLETELY DIFFERENT PATH from DESTROYED_PATH. The sweep really is over every file, and it really fires.

nonBlockingFindings.title: One dead function, one dead class, one dead sentinel.
nonBlockingFindings.detail: is_operation_list (713-719) is never called and is semantically identical to looks_like_operation_list, which is. class Refused (394-395) is never raised and never caught. _ABSENT (513) is never referenced. All three are inert. Named because the dispatch asked specifically whether unreferenced constants or stubs exist: these three are the complete list, and none of them costs a property.

nonBlockingFindings.title: The mutation-suite id sequence skips M38.
nonBlockingFindings.detail: M01..M37 then M39. 38 cases built, 38 counted, no case lost from the total. The only visible trace of the author's interruption.

nonBlockingFindings.title: SHOULD THE SUBJECT BE HARD-CODED? GRADED HERE: YES, RIGHT, and for a reason this instrument makes stronger than the sibling did.
nonBlockingFindings.detail: SUBJECT = 'retention-tiers.v27.json' is a module constant and argv offers no subject path, so the instrument cannot be pointed at retention-tiers.v28. A sibling review graded this RIGHT. It is right here too, and more so.
nonBlockingFindings.why: This instrument is not generic machinery. GATED_PINS names v26/v25/v24 at frozen digests; RECORDED carries 30 measurements of THIS resolution; FREEZE_ANCHORS transcribes 13 sentences of the freeze; the referent map hard-codes eight leaf names of THIS document family; and the delta gate reads RT26-* family names out of THIS artifact's residual block. Pointing it at v28 would not check v28 -- it would compare v28 against v27's frozen measurements and produce a cascade of confidently wrong findings. That is the failure the corpus already recorded when a v26-bound driver was pointed at a v27 document, and the instrument's own delta gate exists precisely to explain those two findings away.
nonBlockingFindings.andTHECOSTISDISCLOSED: The docstring's opening paragraph states the same argument against the PREDECESSOR -- 'check-retention-custody-v26.py carries SUBJECT as a CONSTANT with no subject-selection option ... Section 7.8 is the licence for this file: a NEW CHECKER IS A NEW FILE AND EDITS NOTHING.' The instrument names its own successor cost in its first fifteen lines. That is the correct disposition: v28 needs check-retention-custody-v28.py, not a --subject flag on this one.

nonBlockingFindings.title: Under an executed-closure failure the banner prints 0/0 and None rather than fabricating coverage -- recorded as a STRENGTH that could still mislead.
nonBlockingFindings.detail: chmod 000 on evidence.v10.json (a member of the executed v26 closure) yields a named RT27-DRIVER finding -- 'could not run (PermissionError ...); THE 20 VECTORS AND 24 INVARIANTS WERE NOT EXERCISED and this exit says nothing about them' -- and the banner honestly prints 'vectors 0/0 executed', 'law 14: None cells', 'partition None keys'. Nothing is fabricated. The residual: 'vectors 0/0 executed' scans as a satisfied ratio, and the failure is reported as a FINDING at exit 1 rather than at the distinct exit code 7.8.1 rule 2 prescribes for a per-class named skip.

hostileInputMatrix.method: A byte-for-byte copy of the whole docs/coop tree in a scratch directory, verified to reproduce the live baseline exactly (exit 1, 1 finding, identical text). 100 cases, each mutating exactly ONE file, running the SHIPPED instrument as a subprocess under python3 -I -B, then restoring from pristine. No byte under the real artifacts/ was touched.

PASSES for the GATED class (nothing is parsed at all), for the SUBJECT, and -- notably -- for the executed closure, where a broken member produces a correctly named RT27-DRIVER finding stating that the vectors and invariants were not exercised.

Strings get a negating prefix; digests become 64 f's; ints get +1; bools flip. One full evaluation per leaf, driven in-process against the shipped module by an external driver, finding sets compared against the unmutated base.

escapeRateByTopLevelKey.$.artifact / $.version / $.status / $.da: 0/8 = 0% -- every identity and posture leaf is bound

findingSetDeltaSweep.howToREADTHESENUMBERSHONESTLY: 84% is not a fair headline against the instrument's published 14, because the 14 are CLASSES with worked examples, not a leaf count, and E4/E6/E7/E10 between them account for 811 of the 1047 escapes by naming their blocks wholesale. The instrument told the truth about where its unbound surface is. The finding that survives that correction is OBS-RT27R-02: 43 int/bool leaves escape that no published class covers, and they are not narrative -- they restate quantities the run computes.
findingSetDeltaSweep.whatTHESWEEPCONFIRMSINTHEINSTRUMENTSFAVO: 0 crashes in 1247 same-type falsifications, and every identity, posture, version, status, seal-recommendation and residual-count leaf is bound. The bindings that exist are aimed.

--limits: exit 0, 14 escapes printed, and the count is DERIVED -- print_limits emits len(CAN_I_MAKE_THIS_PASS_ON_A_WRONG_ARTIFACT), not a literal. A published residual count that cannot go stale.

Function-call coverage by sys.settrace across all three modes.
The resolution, re-derived byte-exactly by an independent applier: fc1df558...
The census with bool tested BEFORE int, and the int-first control (788 vs 439).
The type sweep: 966 respellings, 0 admitted, 790 guarded int/bool positions, 0 unruled -- and the 790 reconciled against my own 788 int/bool leaves plus the 2 non-int/bool law-18 controls.
The mutation suite: 38 cases built independently, 0 build failures, 0 no-op mutations, family coverage measured at 16 of 50.

The pin classes: GATED refused at exit 2 in 48 of 48 hostile cases; ADVANCING produced a named non-fatal RT27-PIN-ADVANCED notice and the run continued against live bytes; DESTROYED proved non-vacuous by an external driver against a file at a different path.

The pin-class DERIVATION question: check_recorded_inputs compares the instrument's tables against the artifact's own $.recordedInputsOfThisDeltaFile classification IN BOTH DIRECTIONS -- every literal member must appear in the artifact with matching class AND digest, and every artifact row in neither table is a finding ('an input the artifact depends on is unguarded here'), with all four published cardinalities hard-compared. Standing is cross-derived, not listed. The sibling's `if name in UNSATISFIABLE_PINS` defect is NOT reproduced here.
The second implementation's non-vacuity (4 RT27-XCHECK findings on a keepCount bump) and its ungated denominator (7 -> 0 with zero findings).

The generated referent sweep: 3 findings over the verified predecessor, 0 over the resolved value, 14 rows, 3 strays -- and the instrument raises RT27-SWEEP if the predecessor control returns nothing, so a rule that cannot reproduce the defect it repairs is itself a finding.
RT27-GATE, by executing check-completeness.py's own derivation_declaration() against all 552 files under artifacts/: 13 resolve, exactly 1 refuses, and it is the subject's subject.
Form defect C's independence, by repairing A and B in a copy and measuring that all 8 operations are still refused.
That the resolver does NOT recurse into v26's reviewed bytes.
The exit matrix: no -I / no -B, unknown option, --part with a bad value, --part with no value -- all exit 2 with a named RT27-UNSUPPORTED-INVOCATION saying the check did not run.
whatIDidNotCheck: I did not review retention-tiers.v27.json as a document. Its substantive claims were exercised only through this instrument and through the executed v26 battery. Where those two agree, they agree about a reading -- the instrument says so itself and it is right.
I did not re-derive the 20 vectors or the 24 invariants from first principles. I established that they are DISPATCHED and that their counts are honest; I did not audit what each driver asserts.
I did not re-run the 110-checker corpus sweep the artifact publishes at $.corpusChecksRun, and nothing in this review confirms or contradicts it.

I did not evaluate 561 of the 1811 delta leaves in the falsification sweep -- those under $.corpusChecksRun.perCheckerRecord, whose object keys contain dots. E4 already grades that whole block unbound and my wholesale falsification of it escaped, so the direction is known; the per-leaf rate inside it is not measured.
I did not attempt a COHERENT lie -- a falsehood consistent across every position the instrument compares. The instrument names this as its structural limit 6 and I did not test the bound.

I did not audit check-retention-custody-v26.py itself beyond the two questions I needed from it (how `executed` is counted, and how type_findings defines `guarded`). It is a 281 KB instrument with its own review that I did not read.
I did not test concurrency. RT27-TREE-MOVED was never observed firing; I only established by reading that the selftest path returns above it.

I did not measure whether the artifact's three repairs are the RIGHT repairs. I confirmed 19 is len($.recordedInputs.recorded) and 14 is the Part B UNCHANGED count; whether those are the referents those figures were ever meant to have is the instrument's own structural limit 2 and I inherit it.

I published NO leaf census of this review artifact. 7.2.2 records four measured instances of a self-report that undercounts by exactly its own size, and one reviewer's response -- declining to publish a self-referential count at all -- is the cheapest correct answer. I have taken it.

I did not re-measure the freeze anchors against the pre-drift copy of IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE.md for every run in the hostile matrix. Runs before and after the drift both reported 13/13 folded and 6/6 raw, so no finding in this review turns on which copy was live -- but individual matrix rows were taken against different freeze bytes and I have not partitioned them.
theBoundONTHISREVIEW: I did not write this instrument, its subject, or any predecessor, and I read no lane's report about any of them. Every number here was produced by executing the shipped bytes or by an independent recomputation from the artifacts on disk. That makes this a second measurement rather than a second opinion. It does not make it independent evidence about retention-tiers.v27 itself: 7.8's bound holds unchanged, and what discharges 7.1's DISQUALIFYING residual is an independent re-derivation of the artifact, not another reading of the instrument that checks it. This review narrows nothing and closes nothing.
